movie.title: Savage House
movie.overview: Against the backdrop of 18th century England, a massive pox outbreak, and Jacobite uprising – Sir Chauncey Savage and Lady Savage blindly pursue a better life. It's not without a tinge of irony that their family name is the Savages, for this is a Savage House indeed, filled with duels, decadence, and bloodshed.

reviews.author: CinemaSerf
reviews.content: "Sir Chauncey" (Richard E. Grant) has risen from the pigsty to the elevated world of the landed gentry thanks to a marriage with the impoverished but titled "Lady Savage" (Claire Foy). Having somehow obtained for himself a knighthood, and supported by his ever loyal factotum "Halifax" (Jack Farthing) he lives the life of a gentleman amidst their ever decaying country pile. Then there's a knock at the door. It's a message from the Duke and Duchess of Devonshire. They are making their progress through the county and require board and lodgings for the night. Initially, she concludes that there is no way they can afford to host such luminaries, but he counters that they ought to beg, steal or borrow whatever they need in order to reassert themselves in the all important social order. Such a prestigious visit might also facilitate an advantageous marriage for their mouse-obsessed daughter "Fanny" (Kila Lord Cassidy) too. Reluctantly she agrees and with barely two weeks to go until D-Day they must get their house and their staff fit for purpose. "Sir Chauncey" is a bit of a rake as he chases the maid (Bel Powley) but what he doesn't know is that she is also loved up and conspiring with a butler who is also providing some more intimate services for his mistress whilst helping his boss double-sell various plots of land to the likes of "Mr. Black" (Pip Torrens). With disease rife, duplicity and treachery even more so and the local pheasant (with or without an 'h') population facing decimation this opportunity could prove to be the making of his dynasty, or just as likely, it's doom. There's a lovely rich score to this, the production is sumptuous and some of the dialogue is funny on occasion but the whole thing is just strung out too thinly as we stay only slightly on the right side of farce until a denouement that isn't really a shock to anyone on our side of the screen. Foy and Farthing are underused and though the whole film takes an entertaining enough pop at the ludicrousness of 18th century aristocratic existance and pomposity, I just felt a bit underwhelmed by this hybrid of a "Carry On" romp married to a period piece from Peter Greenaway.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Set in 18th-century England amid a Jacobite uprising and a deadly pox outbreak, Sir Chauncey and Lady Savage navigate a dangerous world of duels, decadence, and bloodshed in a reckless pursuit of social status.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Set against the turbulent backdrop of 18th-century England, Savage House follows Sir Chauncey and Lady Savage as they blindly strive to elevate their fortune. Plagued by a sweeping pox epidemic and the surrounding chaos of the Jacobite rebellion, their path to prosperity is anything but noble. True to their name, the aristocratic couple plunges into a realm defined by deadly duels, dark humor, and unrestrained decadence. Ultimately, their relentless ambition tests just how far they are willing to go to survive in a unforgiving era.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In 18th-century England, society is gripped by political unrest, a terrifying pox epidemic, and the constant threat of the Jacobite uprising. Amidst this national turmoil, Sir Chauncey Savage and his wife, Lady Savage, desperately push for a grander and more luxurious lifestyle. Driven by relentless ambition, their quest for wealth and high social standing draws them into the volatile underbelly of aristocratic life. The Savage household quickly transforms into a battleground of biting political intrigue, dark comedy, and vicious betrayals. Every step forward in their social ascension requires navigating lethal duels, heavy intrigue, and hedonistic excesses. As threats outside their estate escalate with rising rebellion and spreading disease, the chaos inside their home mirrors the madness of the era. The couple must constantly outwit rivals, enemies, and occasionally each other to maintain their precarious position. As blood spills and secrets are weaponized, the hypocrisy of their noble aspirations becomes painfully clear. In the end, Sir Chauncey and Lady Savage prove that their family name is not merely an irony, but an accurate description of their ruthless approach to survival.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Savage House is a dark, satirical period drama that explores the chaotic world of 18th-century English nobility. While the nation reels from a devastating pox outbreak and the violent upheaval of the Jacobite uprising, Sir Chauncey Savage and Lady Savage remain obsessively focused on their own advancement. Unwilling to let societal collapse halt their ambition, the couple plunges into a high-stakes environment filled with lethal duels, illicit affairs, dark humor, and lavish decadence. The story provides a sharp, ironic look at the lengths to which human beings will go for power, contrasting the polished facade of aristocracy with the brutal realities of survival.

story_structure.climax: On the night of the high-stakes dinner gathering, surrounded by absurd preparations and hidden deceit, the long-awaited arrival of their noble guests reaches its turning point.
story_structure.conflict: When a rare opportunity arises to host the influential Duke and Duchess of Devonshire, the Savages plunge into massive debt and desperate preparations to repair their reputation.
story_structure.resolution: The harsh consequences of their blind social ambition and unchecked decadence ultimately unravel the family's future.
story_structure.introduction: In 18th-century England, amid a devastating pox outbreak and the Jacobite uprising, the impoverished Sir Chauncey Savage and his aristocratic wife, Lady Savage, struggle to maintain their crumbling estate and precarious status.
story_structure.risingAction: As the event approaches, internal household betrayals, health crises, duels, and financial ruin threaten to collapse their extravagant facade.

characters.name: Sir Chauncey Savage

characters.name: Lady Savage
characters.description: Sir Chauncey's wickedly ambitious wife who shares his relentless obsession with social standing while engaging in secret betrayals.

characters.description: The family's scheming valet who conducts an affair with Lady Savage and conspires to exploit his employers' financial downfall.

characters.name: Fanny Savage
